story.title: New York Woman Charged with Terrorism for Alleged Capitol Bomb Plot
story.summary: A 35-year-old woman has been charged with a terrorism offense for allegedly plotting to bomb the New York State Capitol. Jessica Bowie reportedly expressed a desire to destroy the Capitol buildings to an FBI informant, leading to her arrest in a sting operation. The charges are linked to her alleged support for the Islamic State (ISIS) group.

explore_lenses.label: Why does the alleged plot matter?
explore_lenses.title: A claimed attack on state government
explore_lenses.summary: The alleged target was not only a public building but the seat of New York’s executive and legislative branches. Officials say there was no immediate ongoing threat after the arrest, while emphasizing security around state government.

claims.text: The Capitol houses the governor’s office and the Senate and Assembly chambers; the complaint alleges Bowie intended to target the building and state senators, making the claimed plot an alleged attack on state institutions as well as people.

Gov. Kathy Hochul said the state had earlier strengthened security at the Capitol and across state government because of political violence and threats against officials, and said there was no immediate threat at the time of the announcement.

The alleged plan to kill senators while they were meeting does not establish that lawmakers would have been present on the intended date; local reporting notes the Legislature is typically in session from January through mid-June.

explore_lenses.label: How did the FBI operation unfold?
explore_lenses.title: A weeks-long informant operation
explore_lenses.summary: The government’s account describes online contact with an FBI confidential source, alleged surveillance of the Capitol, and a controlled August 19 meeting. The devices supplied at that meeting were inert, according to the complaint and reporting.

claims.text: The federal complaint covers alleged conduct from about July 16 through August 19, 2026; reporting based on the filing says Bowie made five visits to Capitol grounds between July 21 and August 9.

According to the complaint, confidential sources posing as ISIS-linked facilitators communicated with Bowie and, at the August 19 meeting, provided what she believed was an explosive device and a firearm; the complaint says both were inert.
FBI Albany Special Agent in Charge Craig Tremaroli characterized the alleged plan as serious and dangerous and credited the Joint Terrorism Task Force with stopping it.
The public record available as of August 21 consists principally of the government’s complaint and law-enforcement statements; Bowie’s Federal Defenders office declined to comment to WXXI/WSKG.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next in the case?
explore_lenses.title: Detention and federal prosecution
explore_lenses.summary: Bowie has made an initial court appearance and is being held pending further proceedings. The case remains at the charging stage, so the government must still prove its allegations beyond a reasonable doubt if it goes to trial.

claims.text: Bowie appeared before U.S. Magistrate Judge Daniel J. Stewart on August 20, 2026, and was ordered detained pending further proceedings.
The complaint charges one count of attempting to provide material support or resources to a designated foreign terrorist organization under 18 U.S.C. § 2339B(a)(1).

DOJ says that charge carries a statutory maximum of 20 years in prison, a fine of up to $250,000, and a potential lifetime term of supervised release; those are maximums, not a prediction of any sentence.
DOJ explicitly states that the complaint is an accusation and that Bowie is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.

story_report.summary: Jessica Bowie, 35, of Albany, New York, has been charged in federal court with attempting to provide material support to ISIS in connection with an alleged plan to bomb the New York State Capitol. Prosecutors say she told an FBI informant she wanted to destroy the Capitol and targeted the building and state senators. Bowie appeared before a U.S. magistrate judge on Aug. 20, 2026, and was ordered held pending further proceedings. The complaint remains an accusation, and Bowie is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

sections.heading: Capitol Target and Alleged Intent
sections.body: The New York State Capitol contains the governor’s office as well as the Senate and Assembly chambers. According to the complaint, Bowie allegedly intended to attack the building and state senators, framing the purported plot as one directed at both state institutions and people. Gov. Kathy Hochul said the state had previously increased security at the Capitol and throughout state government in response to political violence and threats against public officials, and said there was no immediate threat when the case was announced.

sections.heading: Undercover Contacts and Alleged Weapons
sections.body: The federal complaint alleges conduct from about July 16 through Aug. 19, 2026, while local reporting based on the filing says Bowie visited Capitol grounds five times between July 21 and Aug. 9. Prosecutors say confidential sources posing as ISIS-linked facilitators communicated with her and supplied what she believed at an Aug. 19 meeting were an explosive device and firearm. The government says both items were inert; the allegations have not been tested at trial, and Bowie’s Federal Defenders office declined to comment to WXXI/WSKG.

sections.heading: Material Support Charge and Detention
sections.body: Bowie faces one count of attempting to provide material support or resources to a designated foreign terrorist organization, in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 2339B(a)(1). The Justice Department says the charge carries a maximum possible penalty of 20 years in prison, a $250,000 fine and potential lifetime supervised release, though those penalties do not forecast a sentence. She has been detained pending further proceedings.

No indictment, plea, trial date or sentencing outcome was identified in the consulted materials as of Aug. 21, 2026.

related_stories.summary: A charter plane carrying eight people crashed near a U.S. military-managed radar site in western Alaska, resulting in the deaths of all on board. The plane, a Cessna 441, reportedly went down on approach to Cape Newenham. An investigation into the incident is currently underway.

related_stories.title: Personalized mRNA Cancer Treatment Shows Promise Against Melanoma in Trial
related_stories.summary: Merck and Moderna announced that their personalized mRNA cancer treatment has successfully reduced melanoma tumor recurrence in a late-stage clinical trial. This marks a significant milestone in cancer treatment, as it is the first time an mRNA-based drug has shown positive results in such a large trial. Researchers are optimistic about the potential for this approach to be applied to other types of cancer in the future.
